chart.title: Which cities served the most iftar meals
chart.subtitle: Meals distributed during Ramadan food drives, by city
takeaways: New York ranks first in total meals distributed at 50K, followed by Houston (45K) and Los Angeles (40K).
The top three account for 37% of the 359K total shown.
Orlando ranks last at 15K; New York's figure is about 3.4 times as large.
chart.body_md:
*This is sample content. The data is fictional and was created to demonstrate how charts and articles look on this site.*

Every Ramadan, community organizations across the country run food drives that deliver iftar meals and grocery boxes to families in need. This chart compares how many meals were distributed in each city during the month.

## What the data shows

New York ranks first in total meals distributed at 50K, followed by Houston (45K) and Los Angeles (40K). The top three account for 37% of the 359K total shown. Orlando ranks last at 15K; New York's figure is about 3.4 times as large.

## Why it matters

Meal counts show where demand is concentrated and where volunteer networks are strongest. Cities with large totals often have several organizations coordinating distribution, while smaller totals can point to places where more support is needed.

## About this data

Each row is one city. Meals distributed is the total across all participating sites in that city for the full month of Ramadan. All figures are invented for demonstration purposes.

chart.title: Giving surges during Ramadan
chart.subtitle: Combined zakat and sadaqah donations by month, April 2025 to March 2026
takeaways: Total donations rose 320%, from $523K in 2025-04 to $2M in 2026-03.
2026-03 was the highest point in the period.
The lowest point was 2025-07 at $473K.
chart.body_md:
*This is sample content. The data is fictional and was created to demonstrate how charts and articles look on this site.*

Many Muslims time their zakat, the obligatory annual charity, to fall in Ramadan, and voluntary sadaqah tends to rise in the same weeks. This chart tracks combined monthly giving over one year.

## What the data shows

Total donations rose 320%, from $523K in 2025-04 to $2M in 2026-03. 2026-03 was the highest point in the period. The lowest point was 2025-07 at $473K.

## Why it matters

The shape of the year matters for anyone planning a nonprofit budget. A small number of weeks can account for a large share of annual revenue, which affects staffing, campaign timing, and how much cash reserve an organization needs for the rest of the year.

## About this data

Donations are summed across zakat and sadaqah for each calendar month. All figures are invented for demonstration purposes.

chart.body_md:
*This is sample content. The data is fictional and was created to demonstrate how charts and articles look on this site.*

Halal food has moved from specialty grocers into mainstream dining, from fast-casual chains to fine dining. This chart counts new halal restaurant openings each year across six large metro areas.

## What the data shows

Total openings rose 129%, from 82 in 2016 to 188 in 2025. The peak came in 2024 at 191.

## Why it matters

Openings are a useful signal of both consumer demand and investor confidence. A steady rise suggests halal dining is reaching customers well beyond the Muslim community, while dips tend to track wider shocks to the restaurant industry.

## About this data

Openings are counted in the year a restaurant first began serving customers, summed across Houston, Chicago, New York, Dallas, Detroit and Los Angeles. All figures are invented for demonstration purposes.

Texas ranks first in total new centers at 104, followed by California (97) and New York (82). The top three account for 42% of the 668 total shown. Minnesota ranks last at 24; Texas's figure is about 4.3 times as large.

Elementary was highest in 2025 at 31K. High grew fastest, up 68% from 2016 to 2025.

chart.title: Food leads Muslim-owned small businesses

takeaways: Food and restaurants makes up 28% of the total (3,991).
Food and restaurants and Retail together account for 48%.
Construction is the smallest share at 9%.
chart.body_md:
*This is sample content. The data is fictional and was created to demonstrate how charts and articles look on this site.*

Small businesses are a major path to economic mobility for immigrant and second-generation families. This chart shows how Muslim-owned small businesses are spread across sectors in eight large metro areas.

## What the data shows

Across 6 groups totaling 14K: Food and restaurants makes up 28% of the total (3,991). Food and restaurants and Retail together account for 48%. Construction is the smallest share at 9%.

## Why it matters

Sector mix affects everything from access to credit to how exposed businesses are to downturns. Heavy concentration in food and retail means many owners depend on foot traffic and thin margins, while growth in professional services and health care points to a rising share of licensed, higher-income firms.

## About this data

Businesses are grouped by their primary line of work and summed across the eight metro areas. All figures are invented for demonstration purposes.

chart.body_md:
*This is sample content. The data is fictional and was created to demonstrate how charts and articles look on this site.*

Muslim-run free clinics provide primary care, screenings and prescriptions to patients regardless of faith or insurance status. This chart tracks total patient visits across a network of community clinics.

## What the data shows

Total visits rose 195%, from 37K in 2015 to 109K in 2025. 2025 was the highest point in the period.

## Why it matters

Rising visit counts reflect both growing capacity and persistent gaps in access to care. Because most patients are uninsured, clinic volume is also a rough indicator of how many people are falling outside the formal health system in the cities these clinics serve.

## About this data

A visit is one in-person appointment. Patients with several appointments in a year are counted once per appointment. All figures are invented for demonstration purposes.
